# are shown but not run. Set options(FLicc.area_dir = "<folder>") to a folder
# with the OM test set-up and options(FLicc.run_mse = TRUE) to run them.
area_dir <- getOption("FLicc.area_dir", NULL)

# Purpose and scope

This guideline extends the FLicc management procedure (MP) of
[mse-01](mse-01-flicc-modules.html) to stocks whose operating model (OM) has
**areas in the `unit` dimension**: area-specific fleets (gears), area-specific
length samples and catches, movement between areas and a split of
recruitment among them. It documents three levels of spatial resolution in
the MP, from one stock-wide assessment with a fixed split of the TAC to one
assessment, HCR and TAC per area, and the FLicc arguments that switch
between them:

| Module | Argument | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `flicc.sa()` | `unit_fit` | `"pooled"` (default), `"each"`, `"both"` |
| `lbi.hcr()`, `rfb.flicc.hcr()` | `units` | `NULL` (default, stock-wide) or area names |
| `flicc.is()` | `catch_area` | `NULL`, fixed shares by area, or `"recent"` |
| `flicc.is()` | `area_tac` | `"split"` (default) or `"each"` |
| `flicc.is()` | `area_years` | years of catch for `catch_area = "recent"` |

The examples follow the angler-fish test set-up with three areas: area `a`
fished by trawl and gillnet, area `b` by trawl only, and area `c` (gillnet
gear defined, currently unfished) as a closed area.

# Spatial structure in the OM and the OEM

## Areas as units

In the OM every `FLStock` slot carries the areas in `unit`
(`dimnames(stock(om))$unit = c("a", "b", "c")`). The projection method
(`proj_units()` in the test set-up) moves fish between areas, splits
recruitment among them and takes catch targets **by unit**. Gears are
defined by area, each with its own selectivity-at-length, share of the
area's fishing mortality (`f_mult`) and sampling design (`ess_age`,
`ess_len`):

```{r gears, eval = FALSE}
gear_by_area <- list(
  a = list(
    trawl   = list(type = "dnormal", Lpeak = 0.8 * l50, sd_left = 5, sd_right = l50 / 2,
                   f_mult = 0.3, ess_age = 50, ess_len = 300),
    gillnet = list(type = "logistic", L50 = l50, L95 = 1.1 * l50,
                   f_mult = 0.7, ess_age = 50, ess_len = 700)),
  b = list(
    trawl   = list(type = "dnormal", Lpeak = 0.8 * l50, sd_left = 5, sd_right = l50 / 2,
                   f_mult = 1, ess_age = 50, ess_len = 300)),
  c = list(
    gillnet = list(type = "logistic", L50 = l50, L95 = 1.1 * l50,
                   f_mult = 1, ess_age = 50, ess_len = 500)))

om_gears_area <- lapply(gear_by_area, build_gear, lhpar = lh_pars, age = ages,
                        lmin = 5, lmax_mult = 1.5, bin = 3, timing = 0.5)
```

## What the OEM delivers

The area OEM (`sampling.lfd.area.oem()`) samples each gear in each area from
that area's catch-at-age and attaches, as in the single-area case,

* `attr(stk, "lfd")`: `FLQuants` by **gear**, `len x year x unit x ... x iter`,
  with the areas in `unit`. A gear that does not fish in an area has a unit
  of zeros there (`trawl` in `c`, `gillnet` in `b`);
* `attr(stk, "catch_gear")`: catch by gear with reporting error, in the same
  `gear x unit` layout.

This layout is what `flicc.sa()` needs for all three configurations below:
`unitSums()` gives the stock-wide samples, `x[, , "a"]` the samples of one
area.

```
lfd$trawl     unit:  a [samples]   b [samples]   c [zeros]
lfd$gillnet   unit:  a [samples]   b [zeros]     c [zeros: F = 0]
catch_gear    same layout, catch weight by gear and area
```

# Three levels of spatial resolution

```
                      A: pooled, fixed split   B: pooled, recent split   C: per area
flicc.sa(unit_fit =)  "pooled"                 "pooled"                  "each"
  fits per cycle      it                       it                        it x areas with data
  ind                 SPR, LBIspr.trawl, ...   same                      SPR.a, SPR.b, LBIspr.trawl.a, ...
HCR (units =)         NULL                     NULL                      c("a", "b")
  multipliers         one per iteration        one per iteration         one per area and iteration
flicc.is()            area_tac = "split"       area_tac = "split"        area_tac = "each"
                      catch_area = shares      catch_area = "recent"     initac by area
  area TACs           TAC x fixed share        TAC x recent catch share  own TAC x own multiplier
```

| | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status signal | stock-wide | stock-wide | local, per area |
| Distribution of catch among areas | fixed by management | follows the fleets | follows local signals |
| Responds to local depletion | no | no (may even reinforce it) | yes |
| Data needed per area | none | catches | length samples and catches |
| Fit cost per cycle | 1 x | 1 x | number of areas with data |
| Risk | local depletion if shares are wrong | shares drift to where fish are concentrated | noisy local indicators; areas linked by movement |

## A: stock-wide assessment, fixed split

The stock-wide assessment pools all length samples by gear over areas; the
HCR returns one multiplier; `flicc.is()` updates the stock TAC and divides
it by fixed shares, given in unit order or named:

```{r config-a, eval = FALSE}
ctrl_A <- mpCtrl(list(
  est  = mseCtrl(method = flicc.sa, args = list(
           lhpar = flicc_pars, sel_fun = c(trawl = "dsnormal", gillnet = "logistic"),
           m_model = "Gislason", settings = list(obs_model = "dm", CVL = 0.1),
           spr = 40, nyrs = 10, outer_parallel = TRUE)),
  hcr  = mseCtrl(method = lbi.hcr, args = list(
           gear = "SPR", b1 = 0, b2 = 0.35, b3 = 0.45, b4 = 0.7)),
  isys = mseCtrl(method = flicc.is, args = list(
           initac = initac, catch_area = c(a = 0.3, b = 0.7, c = 0)))))
```

Area `c` has a zero share and stays closed.

## B: stock-wide assessment, split by recent catch

Same as A, but the shares are the observed catch shares by area over the
last `area_years` data years, by iteration, taken from
`attr(stk, "catch_gear")` (or `catch(stk)` if the OEM does not attach catch
by gear):

$$
TAC_{u,y} = TAC_y \; \frac{\sum_{t = dy - n + 1}^{dy} C^{obs}_{u,t}}
                        {\sum_{u'} \sum_{t = dy - n + 1}^{dy} C^{obs}_{u',t}} .
$$

```{r config-b, eval = FALSE}
ctrl_B <- ctrl_A
isys(ctrl_B) <- mseCtrl(method = flicc.is, args = list(
  initac = initac, catch_area = "recent", area_years = 3))
```

Because the shares follow the realised catches, which in turn follow the
area TACs, the split is self-reinforcing: it preserves the historical
distribution of the fishery unless the OM's fleets cannot take their TAC in
an area. An area with no recent catch stays closed.

## C: per-area assessments, HCRs and TACs

Each area with length samples is assessed on its own, using only the gears
that fish there (here: trawl and gillnet in `a`, trawl in `b`; `c` has no
samples and is not assessed). The HCR is applied to each area's indicators,
and each area's TAC is updated with its own multiplier:

$$
TAC_{u,y} = TAC_{u,y-frq} \times \text{mult}_{u,y}.
$$

```{r config-c, eval = FALSE}
ctrl_C <- mpCtrl(list(
  est  = mseCtrl(method = flicc.sa, args = list(
           lhpar = flicc_pars, sel_fun = c(trawl = "dsnormal", gillnet = "logistic"),
           refit_sel_fun = c(trawl = "logistic", gillnet = "logistic"),
           m_model = "Gislason", settings = list(obs_model = "dm", CVL = 0.1),
           spr = 40, nyrs = 10, unit_fit = "each", outer_parallel = TRUE)),
  hcr  = mseCtrl(method = lbi.hcr, args = list(
           gear = "SPR", units = c("a", "b"),
           b1 = 0, b2 = 0.35, b3 = 0.45, b4 = 0.7)),
  isys = mseCtrl(method = flicc.is, args = list(
           initac = c(a = 0.3, b = 0.7, c = 0) * initac, area_tac = "each",
           dtaclow = 0.7, dtacupp = 1.2))))
```

Or with the rfb-type rule on each area's gear indicator:

```{r config-c-rfb, eval = FALSE}
hcr(ctrl_C) <- mseCtrl(method = rfb.flicc.hcr, args = list(
  index = "LBIspr.trawl", units = c("a", "b"), spr_trigger = 0.25))
```

`trawl` is the only gear sampled in both areas, so `"LBIspr.trawl"` exists
for `a` and `b`; `"LBIspr.gillnet.b"` exists too, but is `NA` (no gillnet in
`b`), which keeps the TAC of `b` unchanged.

### Names of indicators and tracking metrics

With `unit_fit = "each"` every name gets the area as suffix. For the
example areas:

| Pooled (`"pooled"`) | Per area (`"each"`) |
|---|---|
| `SPR`, `Z`, `Ztgt`, `Zrel` | `SPR.a`, `SPR.b`, `SPR.c`, `Zrel.a`, ... |
| `LBIspr.trawl`, `LBIspr.gillnet` | `LBIspr.trawl.a`, `LBIspr.gillnet.a`, `LBIspr.trawl.b`, ... |
| `LBImean.trawl`, ... | `LBImean.trawl.a`, ... |
| tracking `conv.est`, `used.est`, `sprbound.est`, `refit.est` | `conv.est.a`, `used.est.b`, ... |
| tracking `Lref.trawl`, `Lmeanref.trawl` | `Lref.trawl.a`, `Lmeanref.trawl.b`, ... |
| HCR `mult.hcr`, `decision.hcr`, `trend.hcr` / `r.hcr`, `f.hcr`, `b.hcr` | `mult.hcr.a`, `decision.hcr.b`, ... |
| isys `tac.is` | `tac.is` (sum) and `tac.is.a`, `tac.is.b`, `tac.is.c` |

`mp()` also tracks every indicator as `<name>.ind` in the last data year.
Gears absent from an area are present with `NA`, so the same names exist in
every area; an area without any samples (here `c`) has `NA` throughout and
`used.est.c = 0`, without a warning.

### How the modules connect

```
flicc.sa(unit_fit = "each")
   for u in units:  lfd[, , u], catch_gear[, , u]  ->  drop gears without samples
                    ->  fiticc() per iteration       ->  ind: <name>.u
lbi.hcr(units = c("a","b"))  /  rfb.flicc.hcr(units = ...)
   for u in units:  trend on ind[[<gear>.u]], status on ind[["SPR.u"]]
                    ->  track mult.hcr.u, decision.hcr.u
   ctrl = mean of the unit multipliers (information only)
flicc.is(area_tac = "each")
   for u in units:  prev = initac[u] or tac.is.u at ay - frq
                    mult = mult.hcr.u (stock-wide ctrl value if not tracked)
                    TAC_u = prev x mult, limits with decision.hcr.u
   Cmax on the sum (proportional scaling)
   ctrl = one row per management year and unit
```

The per-area multipliers travel from the HCR to `flicc.is()` through the
tracking object (`mult.hcr.<unit>`), in the same way as `decision.hcr`
already did, so the `ctrl` returned by the HCR stays a single row.

## Pooled and per-area fits together: `unit_fit = "both"`

`"both"` returns the pooled indicators and the per-area indicators in the
same `ind`. The HCRs use one or the other (`units = NULL` or area names).
This is useful to monitor both scales in the same run, e.g. to see whether
a stock-wide rule (A or B) hides local depletion, at the cost of the extra
fits. Combining them in one rule, such as an area trend with a stock-wide
SPR safeguard, is not implemented yet.

# What a per-area assessment measures

A length-based catch-curve model treats the length composition as the
equilibrium outcome of growth, natural mortality, fishing mortality and
selectivity **within one closed population**. An area of a stock with
movement is not closed:

* **Movement.** Fish that grow up in one area and move to another carry the
  exploitation history of both. With movement from `a` to `b`, the large
  fish in `b` have been exposed to F in `a` as well, and the per-area SPR is
  an *apparent* local SPR, not the SPR of a sub-population. With strong
  mixing, per-area estimates converge to the stock-wide one, plus noise.
* **Ontogenetic movement.** If small fish dominate one area and large fish
  another, the per-area compositions mix growth and movement. The model
  will absorb this in selectivity or in Z, and the local indicator is biased
  in a direction set by the movement pattern. The OM is the place to test
  whether the per-area indicators still rank areas correctly.
* **Recruitment split.** The relative recruitment to each area does not
  enter the per-recruit indicators; an area receiving few recruits can show
  a high SPR at a very low abundance.
* **Data per area.** Each area's fit needs enough length samples and enough
  gear contrast. Area `b` has a single dome-shaped gear, where F and the
  descending limb of selectivity are confounded; `refit_sel_fun` with
  asymptotic selectivity and the SPR boundary check (`spr_max`) are
  important there, and `used.est.b` should be monitored.
* **Life history.** All areas share `lhpar`. Area differences in growth or
  M are not represented by the estimator.

Configuration C is therefore most useful where movement among areas is
limited (e.g. seamounts or banks) and local depletion is the main risk;
with strong mixing, A or B with a stock-wide assessment is simpler and has
less noise.

# Requirements for the OM projection

`flicc.is()` returns a `fwdControl` with **one row per management year and
area** whenever areas are used (`catch_area` given or `area_tac = "each"`):

```{r ctrl-structure, eval = FALSE}
fwdControl(unlist(lapply(mys, function(y)
  lapply(units, function(u)
    list(year = y, quant = "catch", unit = u, value = tac_u[u, ]))),
  recursive = FALSE))
```

The projection method of the OM (`proj_units()` in the test set-up) must

* take catch targets by `unit`, including zero targets for closed areas;
* accept several management years per cycle when `frq > 1` (the same TAC is
  repeated in every year of the cycle);
* handle a stock-wide target without `unit` when `catch_area = NULL`.

# Summarising runs by area

```{r summarise, eval = FALSE}
library(data.table)
trk <- run_C@tracking
areas <- c("a", "b", "c")

## area TACs, area SPR and share of usable fits
dt <- trk[metric %in% c(paste0("tac.is.", areas), paste0("SPR.", areas, ".ind"),
                        paste0("used.est.", areas))]
dt[, area := sub(".*\\.([abc])(\\.ind)?$", "\\1", metric)]
dt[, what := sub("\\.[abc](\\.ind)?$", "", metric)]

ggplot(dt, aes(factor(year), data)) +
  geom_boxplot(outliers = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(what ~ area, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = NULL)

## true SSB by area in the OM
stks <- FLStocks(lapply(setNames(nm = areas), function(u) run_C@om@stock[, , u]))
plot(stks) + facet_wrap(~qname, scales = "free_y")
```

# Notes on the angler-fish test set-up

Points found while going through `OEM_lfd_setup_flicc.R`:

* **HCR argument typo.** `lbi.hcr(..., b = 0, b2 = 0.35, ...)` passes `b`
  into `...`, where it is ignored, so `b1` stays at its default of 0.1.
  Use `b1 = 0` for the v1 rule.
* **Gear names.** `sel_fun = c(Trawl = "dsnormal", Gillnet = "logistic")` is
  named with capitals while the OEM gears are `trawl` and `gillnet`.
  `flicc.sa()` now matches `sel_fun`, `refit_sel_fun` and `ess.g` by gear
  name when all gears are named and falls back to gear order otherwise, so
  this still works, but lower-case names avoid the ambiguity.
* **Area shares.** `catch_area = c(0.3, 0.7, 0)` is read in unit order
  (`a`, `b`, `c`); named shares are safer.
* **Parallel `mp()`.** The length-sampling deviances are lists of plain
  arrays. When `mp(parallel = TRUE)` splits iterations across workers it
  subsets only `FLQuant` deviances (see the FLRef developer notes), so
  each worker may reuse the draws of iterations `1:length(chunk)`. This does
  not bias the results, but iterations in different chunks then share their
  sampling draws. Run with `parallel = FALSE` in `mp()` and
  `parallel = TRUE, workers = n` in `flicc.sa()` until the OEM deviances are
  `FLQuant`s.
* **Fit cost.** `unit_fit = "each"` fits areas `a` and `b` (two models per
  iteration and cycle; `c` is skipped). With `nyrs = 10` and 50 projection
  years at `frq = 1`, this doubles the run time of configuration A.

# Appendix: arguments for multiple areas

| Function | Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flicc.sa()` | `unit_fit` | `"pooled"` | `"pooled"`: sum over units; `"each"`: one fit per unit with data; `"both"` |
| `flicc.sa()` | `sel_fun`, `refit_sel_fun`, `ess.g` | | by gear name (all gears named) or in gear order; subset to the gears of each unit |
| `lbi.hcr()` | `units` | `NULL` | apply the rule to `<gear>.<unit>` and `SPR.<unit>` |
| `rfb.flicc.hcr()` | `units` | `NULL` | apply the rule to `<index>.<unit>`, `<f>.<unit>`, `SPR.<unit>` |
| `flicc.is()` | `area_tac` | `"split"` | `"split"`: stock TAC divided among units; `"each"`: TAC per unit from `mult.hcr.<unit>` |
| `flicc.is()` | `catch_area` | `NULL` | shares by unit (named or unit order) or `"recent"` |
| `flicc.is()` | `area_years` | 3 | data years for `catch_area = "recent"` |
| `flicc.is()` | `initac` | | stock total, or by unit for `area_tac = "each"` |
| `flicc.is()` | `Cmax` | `NA` | cap on the stock total; area TACs scaled proportionally |
